Subject: Flat viewings while I'm away

Dear Tavin,

Thank you for getting in touch, and for laying out the options so clearly — I really appreciate it.

I'm happy for you to put the flat on the viewing list. I'll be away from 6 to 20 November, and since you have a spare key, please feel free to go ahead with accompanied viewings during that period. I'd be grateful if you could let me know the dates and times in advance so I'm aware of when people will be in the flat.

As you know, I'd normally prefer to be home when strangers visit, but I don't want to make the letting process more difficult than it needs to be, so this seems like a reasonable arrangement.

Thanks again for being so accommodating, and for confirming that the choice won't affect my tenancy or deposit.

Best regards,
[Your name]

I am writing regarding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June at [address].

As you know, I removed all of my belongings and vacated the flat on 31 May, and I was not living there at any point in June. I returned all keys to your office on 8 June, which was the earliest date I was able to get there. I understand that under our signed agreement rent continues until the day the keys are returned, and I appreciate that the June charge reflects this.

Nonetheless, since the flat was empty and I made no use of it during those eight days, I would be very grateful if you would consider refunding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June as a goodwill gesture. If you are able to do so, please send the refund to my usual account, the details of which you already hold.

Thank you for your understanding, and for your help throughout my tenancy. I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Contact details]

Note: By your own account the agreement entitles her to rent through 8 June, so the letter asks for a goodwill refund rather than claiming one is owed.

Dear Orla,

Thank you for sending through the moving-out details – everything's clear, and I'm getting organised for the 30th.

I wanted to ask whether you'd be happy for me to repaint the living room the weekend before I leave. I'd use the original pale grey so it matches what was there when I moved in. I know your decorator is already booked for 2 July, so please don't feel you need to say yes on my account – I'd just like to hand the place back looking as cared for as I can, and I'm glad to do the work and cover the paint myself.

If you'd rather I left the walls as they are for the decorator, that's completely fine too – just let me know what suits you.

Thanks again for being such an easy landlord to rent from. I've really enjoyed living here.

Best wishes,
[Your name]

Note: Since her decorator will repaint the whole room on 2 July regardless, your repaint would be covered over two days later – you might get the same goodwill from a thorough clean and filling any nail holes instead.

Subject: Reading support for Seli

Dear Ms. Dalven,

I hope you're well. I'm writing about my daughter, Seli, in your class this year.

Seli really enjoys stories and is keen on books at home, but she tends to lose confidence when asked to read aloud, and I think a little extra encouragement would help her a great deal.

Would it be possible to arrange a short weekly practice session for her during the normal class reading period? Even ten or fifteen minutes of focused reading-aloud practice with some gentle support would, I believe, make a real difference to how she feels about it.

Thank you very much for considering this. I'm happy to talk further or help in any way I can.

Kind regards,
[Your name]

Please let me know if this would be feasible, or if there's anything I should do to support this at home. Thank you very much for your time and for all you do for the class.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Contact details]
